slides.title: Eco3S: Complex Socio-Economic System Simulation via Agent-Based Models
slides.tldr: SOCIO-ECONOMIC SYSTEM SIMULATION FRAMEWORK
slides.highlight: Eco3S introduces a framework for socio-economic simulation using LLM-based agents and co-evolving environments, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: Eco3S is an LLM-based framework for simulating complex socio-economic systems with co-evolving environments and causal reasoning.
card.key_idea: Combines co-evolving agent-environment feedback loops, SCM-inspired structural causal simulation for counterfactuals, and a Simulation-Analysis-Refinement (SAR) paradigm to automate simulation design and optimization.
card.evaluation: Replicated three economic studies (canal decay, governance origins, information propagation) and four phenomena. Results aligned with empirical benchmarks and outperformed baseline simulations.
card.limitation: LLM reasoning remains a 'black box' lacking transparency, and validity is difficult to evaluate without existing historical benchmarks.

slides.title: CoRenew: A large language model agent-based policy simulation platform for multifamily residential redevelopment
slides.tldr: LLM-BASED POLICY SIMULATION FOR RESIDENTIAL REDEVELOPMENT
slides.highlight: CoRenew uses LLM-based agents to simulate stakeholder negotiations and evaluate policy effects, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: CoRenew is an LLM-agent-based platform for simulating multi-round negotiations to evaluate multifamily residential redevelopment policies.
card.key_idea: It uses LLM agents structured by the Theory of Planned Behavior for residents, alongside rule-based planner and developer agents, to simulate adaptive negotiations.
card.evaluation: Validated against 324 resident surveys and a real-world case; achieved 100% directional agreement and 94.7% statistical significance across 19 structural paths.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Not Forgotten: Implementation and Evaluation of a Personalized Episodic Memory for the Humanoid Robot Head Kim
slides.tldr: EPISODIC MEMORY ENHANCES SOCIAL ROBOT TRUSTWORTHINESS
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that a personalized episodic memory module for a humanoid robot head increases perceived sociability, warmth, and trustworthiness. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Episodic memory in a humanoid robot head increases perceived sociability without increasing user disturbance.
card.key_idea: A lightweight module using vector-based semantic retrieval and a hybrid scoring function (combining cosine similarity, recency, access frequency, and emotional intensity) to inject past interactions into LLM prompts.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects video-based study (N=43) using the HRIES scale; results showed significant gains in trustworthiness (d=0.62) and warmth (d=0.56).
card.limitation: Video-based format lacked real-time interaction, and the study did not compare the hybrid architecture against simpler retrieval methods.

slides.title: Belief-Aware Influence and Trust (BAIT): Shaping Human Belief During Repeated Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: OPTIMIZING HUMAN TRUST IN REPEATED HRI
slides.highlight: The BAIT controller manages the trade-off between long-term influence and human trust during repeated interactions, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: BAIT balances long-term influence and human trust to maintain robot task performance during repeated interactions.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical particle filter tracks short-term strategies and long-term beliefs, feeding a belief-aware MPPI planner that optimizes the trade-off between unpredictability (influence) and transparency (trust).
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulations, a human-subject study, and real-world GEM vehicle lane-merging; compared against Stackelberg baselines using task performance and user trust metrics.
card.limitation: The approach relies on a structured human model and specific latent state assumptions to maintain computational tractability.

slides.title: Partner Capability Estimation for Task-Agnostic Adaptation in Ad-Hoc Teamwork
slides.tldr: TASK-AGNOSTIC PARTNER CAPABILITY ESTIMATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces CE-CM and CE-CM-Div to infer hidden partner capabilities online, supporting the ADAM-CHAT goal of agents that adapt at test time and infer partner intent for ad-hoc human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: A Bayesian method for agents to infer task-invariant partner capabilities and adapt coordination across multiple tasks.
card.key_idea: CE-CM uses simulation-based approximate Bayesian computation to infer latent capability vectors from joint trajectories, inducing capability-conditioned models for joint planning with decentralized execution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in TidyUP (PDDL) and Overcooked (simulator) using simulated partners and 225 human trajectories; CE-CM-Div improved estimates for human partners.
card.limitation: Standard CE-CM is brittle when partners act sub-optimally or follow diverse strategies not captured by a single optimal trajectory.

slides.title: Teachy Mini: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of a Knowledge-Based Generative Social Robot for Higher Education
slides.tldr: KNOWLEDGE-BASED GENERATIVE SOCIAL ROBOT FOR TUTORING
slides.highlight: This work explores the use of knowledge-based design and retrieval-augmented generation to create a generative social robot for personalized tutoring, aligning with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

card.one_liner: Teachy Mini is a generative social robot using Knowledge-Based Design to provide responsible, personalized tutoring in higher education.
card.key_idea: Operationalizes KBD requirements via dynamic system prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for lecture slides, and stateful prompt orchestration to manage pedagogical dialogue states.
card.evaluation: Between-subjects study (N=24) comparing KBD vs. control robot. Teachy Mini was perceived as significantly more responsible, though learning gains and acceptance showed no significant differences.
card.limitation: Preliminary evaluation with a small sample size (N=24) and limited to a single-session interaction context.

slides.title: StARS: Socially Appropriate Robot Actions via a Recommender System-Driven Approach
slides.tldr: PERSONALIZED SOCIAL ROBOT ACTIONS
slides.highlight: StARS uses a recommender system-driven approach to generate user-specific appropriateness scores for robot actions, supporting the RwB goal of embodied social robots that align with individual human norms.

card.one_liner: StARS uses a recommender system approach to personalize socially appropriate robot actions based on individual user preferences.
card.key_idea: A model-agnostic framework integrating collaborative filtering (matrix factorization) with learnable scene representations via residual fusion to predict user-specific appropriateness scores for candidate robot actions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MannersDB+ and SocNav1 using various backbones (MLPs, GNNs). Results show statistically significant improvements in RMSE/MSE, Pearson r, and CCC.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: Low-Latency Turn-Taking via Context-Aware Preface Generation in a Real-World Dialogue Robot
slides.tldr: CONTEXT-AWARE PREFACE GENERATION FOR LOW-LATENCY DIALOGUE
slides.highlight: This work proposes a two-stage incremental framework using an intent readiness detector and voice activity projection to reduce response latency. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and listener modeling within human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: A two-stage framework reduces robot response latency using context-aware prefaces instead of generic fillers.
card.key_idea: An intent readiness detector triggers a short LLM-generated prefatory response based on partial input, while a Voice Activity Projection model determines the optimal speech onset timing.
card.evaluation: Field experiment with a route-guidance robot in a mall. Compared no-filler, fixed-filler, and contextual-preface conditions using latency metrics and 7-point Likert scales.
card.limitation: Prefatory and main responses are generated independently, leading to potential semantic/prosodic discontinuity and occasional dialogue breakdowns like fragments or generic questions.

slides.title: Extended Reality as a Mediation Layer for Situated Human Control in Human-Robot Teaming
slides.tldr: XR FOR SITUATED HUMAN-ROBOT CONTROL
slides.highlight: This work proposes using Extended Reality (XR) as a mediation layer to improve human control and accountability of robot autonomy in dynamic environments, supporting the RwB focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Proposes Extended Reality (XR) as a bidirectional mediation layer for situated human control in human-robot teaming.
card.key_idea: XR mediates between human intent and robot autonomy via four functions: grounding multimodal input, contextualizing plans, clarifying shared control levels, and managing team roles and recovery.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated; the paper outlines a research agenda and suggests evaluation metrics like correction latency and plan comprehension for future studies.
card.limitation: The paper is a position piece providing a conceptual framework and design dimensions rather than an empirical implementation or validation.

slides.title: Let Me Look at You: Advanced Facial Expression Modeling for Conversational Speech Synthesis
slides.tldr: FACIAL-EXPRESSION-AWARE CONVERSATIONAL SPEECH SYNTHESIS
slides.highlight: This work introduces FacialTalker and the VSDD-1K dataset to integrate facial expression modeling into conversational speech synthesis, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: FacialTalker enhances conversational speech synthesis by incorporating user facial expressions via a novel visual tokenizer.
card.key_idea: An LLM-based framework using AUTokenizer to discretize facial Action Units into single tokens and DualDPO to jointly optimize visual and speech preferences.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on VSDD-1K, MultiDialog, and AvaMERG using objective metrics (F1, SIM, PDTW) and subjective MOS scores; outperformed strong baselines.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: WCM: World-Cognition Model for Generalizable Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: HUMAN-CENTERED EMBODIED AGENT FOR INTERACTIVE TEACHING
slides.highlight: The World-Cognition Model introduces a human-in-the-loop teaching mode and a concurrent runtime for reasoning and dialogue, supporting the RwB goal of AI-mediated embodied learning.

card.one_liner: WCM is a human-centered robot agent enabling real-time interaction, correction, and learning via a modular architecture.
card.key_idea: Uses SLAK (Sensing, Logic, Action, Knowledge) architecture with an asynchronous runtime and a CoT distillation pipeline to learn from autonomous rollouts and human teaching.
card.evaluation: Tested on a low-cost mobile-manipulator across nine real-world HRI tasks, achieving a 73.8% average success rate including held-out tasks.
card.limitation: Currently limited by hardware constraints and a case-study based evaluation approach.

slides.title: ACME: A Multi-Cultural, Multi-Embodiment Social-Navigation Dataset
slides.tldr: MULTI-CULTURAL SOCIAL NAVIGATION DATASET
slides.highlight: This dataset captures goal-driven social navigation and human-robot interactions across diverse cultures and embodiments, supporting the development of social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: ACME is a large-scale, multi-cultural, multi-embodiment dataset for social robot navigation and pedestrian trajectory prediction.
card.key_idea: Data collected across 5 countries using 7 robot embodiments, featuring 29.35 hours of onboard robot data and 43.5 hours of overhead pedestrian tracking with speech interactions.
card.evaluation: Compared against prior datasets via qualitative/quantitative analysis of scenario complexity and pedestrian behavior; benchmarked state-of-the-art vision navigation and trajectory prediction models.
card.limitation: Varying IRB privacy requirements led to different anonymization levels (face blurring to full body segmentation), causing some loss of identifying features.

slides.title: Indic DiarBench: A Multilingual Joint Diarization and ASR Benchmark for Indian Languages
slides.tldr: MULTILINGUAL DIARIZATION AND ASR BENCHMARK
slides.highlight: This benchmark provides human-corrected, multi-speaker audio across 22 Indian languages, supporting HyECHO's focus on diarization and social perception in complex conversational settings.

card.one_liner: Indic DiarBench is a new benchmark for joint speaker diarization and ASR across 22 Indian languages.
card.key_idea: A 108-hour corpus of human-corrected, speaker-attributed transcriptions from near-field, far-field, and in-the-wild audio, capturing code-mixing, dialectal variation, and speaker overlap.
card.evaluation: Evaluated commercial APIs, multimodal LLMs, and an Indic-specialized system using DER, cpWER, and WDER; Sarvam AI achieved the best overall results.
card.limitation: The in-the-wild subset only covers 10 of 22 languages and lacks speaker IDs; designed for evaluation, not training.

slides.title: STEER: Steerable Dyadic Head Avatars
slides.tldr: CONTROLLABLE DYADIC MOTION FOR CONVERSATIONAL AVATARS
slides.highlight: STEER provides explicit control over gaze, head rhythm, and emotion in dyadic head avatars, contributing to HyECHO's focus on modeling engagement and listener behavior.

card.one_liner: STEER is a controllable 3D dyadic motion prior for photorealistic, reactive conversational head avatars.
card.key_idea: A causal flow-matching transformer generates partner-aware motion conditioned on audio and explicit semantic controls for gaze, head-rhythm, and emotion, driving a Gaussian avatar via a learned translator.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a filtered RealTalk corpus against DualTalk, UniLS, and DiffPoseTalk using lip-sync, motion realism (vFDE), dynamics (FDD), and diversity metrics.
card.limitation: Behavioral labels are derived from kinematic proxies via an annotation pipeline rather than ground-truth social-intent labels.

slides.title: Towards Reducing Foreign Language Anxiety Using Level-Appropriate Embodied Conversational Agents
slides.tldr: LEVEL-APPROPRIATE EMBODIED CONVERSATIONAL AGENTS FOR SLA
slides.highlight: This work proposes a multi-agent system that adapts dialogue complexity to a user's proficiency level to reduce foreign language anxiety, contributing to HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A multi-agent system generating CEFR level-appropriate dialogue to help reduce foreign language anxiety in learners.
card.key_idea: A "generate-evaluate-regenerate" loop using multiple LLM agents and a level classifier to adapt dialogue simplicity to user proficiency.
card.evaluation: Pilot study with Japanese university students; 87.4% of output matched CEFR levels versus 54.1% for unsimplified agents.
card.limitation: Small sample size resulted in no statistically significant evidence that the system reduces foreign language anxiety levels.

slides.title: AtmosERC: Modeling Dialogue-Level Affective Atmosphere for Emotion Recognition in Conversation
slides.tldr: DIALOGUE-LEVEL AFFECTIVE ATMOSPHERE MODELING
slides.highlight: This work introduces AtmosERC to capture dialogue-level affective atmosphere and speaker-conditioned priors, contributing to the multimodal social perception of engagement and emotion patterns relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: AtmosERC improves conversation emotion recognition by using a dialogue-level affective atmosphere as a global prior.
card.key_idea: It extracts a stable affective atmosphere vector via relation-aware graph filtering from RoBERTa features, providing a global prior for local emotion decoding or LLM prompting.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on IEMOCAP, MELD, EmoryNLP, and DailyDialog against sequence, transformer, graph, and LLM baselines; results show consistent improvements over global context pooling.
card.limitation: A gap exists between predicted atmosphere descriptors and gold-proxy dominant emotions, indicating room for improvement in atmosphere estimation.

slides.title: Lag-aware cross-hand alignment for dual-hand action segmentation
slides.tldr: LAG-AWARE DUAL-HAND ACTION SEGMENTATION
slides.highlight: The LACA module improves dual-hand action segmentation by estimating temporal-offset distributions between hand-specific feature streams. This supports the MOSAIC goal of estimating human proficiency through ego-exo views and aligning human-AI intent.

card.one_liner: LACA improves dual-hand action segmentation by explicitly aligning asynchronous hand transitions using time-varying temporal offsets.
card.key_idea: A lightweight module estimating bidirectional offset distributions with a learned null state to suppress irrelevant cross-hand transfers, supervised by compatibility-aware targets derived from training annotations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HA-ViD and ATTACH datasets; improved two-hand mean F1@50 and boundary F1 over Polyphony baseline. Results are seed-averaged and consistent.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.

slides.title: SymmGrid: Super-Scaling On-Robot Learning with Parallelized Symmetries and Egocentric-Exocentric Visual Perception
slides.tldr: ACCELERATING ON-ROBOT LEARNING VIA SYMMETRIC DATA AUGMENTATION
slides.highlight: SymmGrid utilizes parallelized symmetries and both egocentric and exocentric visual perception to accelerate on-robot learning for manipulation tasks. This approach to multi-view perception and training efficiency is relevant to the MOSAIC project's focus on ego-exo views and skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: SymmGrid accelerates on-robot reinforcement learning by super-scaling data through parallelized branched symmetries and visual warping.
card.key_idea: A trajectory-level augmentation framework that models MDPs as symmetry trees, using affine transformations to create geometric grids of state-action pairs and homographies for exocentric visual invariance.
card.evaluation: Tested on real Franka robots (peg-insertion, cable routing, object relocation) against SERL; showed 1.37-2.17x training speedups and up to 2.59x nAUC improvement.
card.limitation: Exocentric visual warping via homographies can produce artifacts in certain scenes and assumes a planar representation.

slides.title: Proceedings of The First Reflection in Creative Experience (RiCE) Workshop
slides.tldr: REFLECTION AND METACOGNITION IN CREATIVE AI
slides.highlight: This workshop examines reflection and metacognition in creative interaction, which is relevant to ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction via meta-cognition.

card.one_liner: Proceedings of an interdisciplinary workshop focused on reflection and metacognition in creative user experiences.
card.key_idea: Establishing a community and shared frameworks for studying and designing reflection within creative interactions, spanning HCI, AI, cognitive science, and digital art.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated.
card.limitation: Not clearly stated.
